items.briefing:
Security researchers are warning that cybercriminals are now using calendar invitation files (.ics) to deliver phishing attacks. These fake invites can appear in your email or calendar app looking like legitimate meeting requests, but clicking links inside them may lead to credential theft or malware. This is a timely reminder to be cautious with unexpected calendar invites, especially from unfamiliar senders.

On the industry side, Australian financial services organisations are reportedly ahead of other sectors in AI-related identity security readiness, though gaps remain across the broader economy. ScamWatch continues to flag active scam activity targeting Australians.

**Tip:** If you receive an unexpected calendar invite with a link, don't click it — verify the meeting request directly with the sender through a separate channel.
